defects.title: The two densities are compared on different grids, so distinct populations get a zero distance
defects.trigger: x = [1.0; 2.0; 2.5; 4.0; 5.5; 6.0]; KLdistance(x, x + 100, 1, {'a'}) (two populations with disjoint supports); also KLdistance(x, 3 * x, 1, {'a'})
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) dist = 1.32646e-30 for x and x + 100 and 2.08731e-31 for x and 3 * x, i.e. zero up to rounding: cobraKsdensity evaluates each density on 100 points spanning its own sample (grids [-4.76, 11.76] and [95.24, 111.76] here) and lines 34-35 and 47-48 discard the grid (xi); the two density vectors are equal (max difference 3.2e-16), so KLDis (lines 36 and 50) compares values at unrelated x points. The permutation distances (lines 39-51) share the error
defects.expected: the Kullback-Leibler distance between the two distributions, i.e. the two densities evaluated on one common grid: a clearly positive distance for disjoint or rescaled populations

notes: independent review T021: finding confirmed (WRONG verdict). The two densities are evaluated by cobraKsdensity on grids spanning each sample's own range and the grid output is discarded, so KLDis compares values at unrelated x points; the former oracles re-ran the same pairing and reproduced the defect. Reproduction (R2025a, 2026-11-17): x = [1.0; 2.0; 2.5; 4.0; 5.5; 6.0]; KLdistance(x, x + 100, 1, {'a'}) -> 1.32646e-30; KLdistance(x, 3 * x, 1, {'a'}) -> 2.08731e-31; [f1, xi1] = cobraKsdensity(x); [f2, xi2] = cobraKsdensity(x + 100); max(abs(f1 - f2)) -> 3.2e-16 with xi1 = [-4.76, 11.76], xi2 = [95.24, 111.76] (close the figures afterwards). Test converted to the quarantine layout. Reach: every call form (the first distance and every permutation distance use the separate grids for any data). src callers of KLdistance: none (grep 'KLdistance(' in src finds only the function itself). Callees KLDis and cobraKsdensity behave as documented; the defect is the pairing in KLdistance.
confirmed_by: lead (independent review T021 finding; writer's MATLAB reproduction: shifted and scaled copies give distance ~1e-30, densities on separate grids)

defects.title: the version flag and the compiler options are never passed to mex
defects.trigger: generateMexFastFVA(root, 0) with a complete CPLEX installation (include and library folders and libcplex.a), any CPLEX version
defects.observed: MATLAB R2025a 2026-11-17 (mex replaced by a stand-in that records its arguments): the compilation call receives the eight arguments -output, cplexFVA128, -largeArrayDims, -ldl, CFLAGS="\$CFLAGS", -I"<include>", "<source>", <library>; the variable CFLAGS of line 138 (with -DHIGHER_THAN_128 or -DLOWER_THAN_128, -O3, -Werror, ...) is never used, because line 139 writes the literal text \$CFLAGS. cplexFVA.c is therefore compiled with neither version macro, which leaves out its CPLEX log-file code (lines 1140-1153 of cplexFVA.c), so the MEX file writes no CPLEX log file (inferred from the C source; nothing compiled here, CPLEX is not installed)
defects.expected: mex called with the flags of line 138 (CFLAGS="$CFLAGS <flags>"), so that the version switch of lines 79-86 takes effect

defects.title: CPLEX 12.10 and later 12.1x versions are classed as older than 12.8
defects.trigger: generateMexFastFVA(root, 0) with ILOG_CPLEX_PATH and root under .../CPLEX_Studio1210/cplex (version string 1210)
defects.observed: MATLAB R2025a 2026-11-17: lines 54-56 turn 1210 into 121, which is below 128, so versionFlag is -DLOWER_THAN_128 and versionVS is vs2013 (lines 80-86). On Linux and macOS this changes nothing (stand-in mex: the command is that of 12.8 apart from the output name cplexFVA1210) because the flag never reaches mex (defect above); on Windows the library is looked for in lib\x64_windows_vs2013\stat_mda (line 97; read from the code, not run)
defects.expected: 12.10 classed as 12.8 or later (-DHIGHER_THAN_128 and the library folder of that CPLEX release)

notes: independent review T021: finding reproduced only in part, not as a wrong-result. Confirmed: 1210 / 10 = 121 < 128, so CPLEX 12.10 gets versionFlag -DLOWER_THAN_128 and versionVS vs2013. Not reproduced: the claimed consequence (compiling with -DLOWER_THAN_128 and -Werror). With mex replaced by a recording stand-in (a mex.m first on the path; MATLAB warns it shadows a built-in), the compilation call receives exactly {-output, cplexFVA<version>, -largeArrayDims, -ldl, CFLAGS="\$CFLAGS", -I"<include>", "<source>", <library>} for 12.8, 12.9, 12.10, 12.6.3 and 20.1 alike: line 139 writes the literal text \$CFLAGS, so the CFLAGS variable of line 138 (version flag, -O3, -Werror) never reaches mex for any version and cplexFVA.c is compiled with neither LOWER_THAN_128 nor HIGHER_THAN_128, which compiles out its CPLEX log-file code (cplexFVA.c lines 1140-1153; inferred from the C source, nothing compiled, CPLEX not installed). Recorded (1) flags never passed to mex as wrong-result (lead decision 2026-11-17, R5: the computed version flag never reaches mex, contradicting the code's evident intent on a valid call) and (2) the 12.10 misclassification as limitation, whose only remaining effect is the Windows library folder lib\\x64_windows_vs2013\\stat_mda (read from code; a stand-in isunix/ismac run failed earlier inside other functions, so Windows was not run). Test converted to the quarantine layout (header entries kept; the stand-in mex checks, with a temporary CBTDIR holding a copy of compatMatrix.rst, are described in its Purpose for when the defect is fixed; they passed before the conversion). Also seen, not filed (callee or unverifiable): getCobraSolverVersion ignores its documented third input rootPathSolver and reads the version from ILOG_CPLEX_PATH, so generateMexFastFVA(root) with ILOG_CPLEX_PATH unset or pointing elsewhere names the MEX file cplexFVAundetermined (observed with the stand-in) or cplexFVA (empty path) - a defect of getCobraSolverVersion; the Windows library file name for 4-digit versions gets no added zero (cplex1210.lib), and src/analysis/FVA/fastFVA/mex/README.txt says CPLEX 12.9 on Windows uses x64_windows_vs2017, which neither branch of lines 80-86 selects (Windows only, real layout not verifiable here). Reach: none - no src function calls generateMexFastFVA (fastFVA only names it in messages).
confirmed_by: lead (review T021; writer's reproduction with a recording stand-in mex: line 139 passes the literal CFLAGS="\$CFLAGS", the computed version flag never reaches mex; raised to wrong-result by research R5, evident intent)

defects.title: The documented defaults of maxMetConn, maxNumPnts and LoopRxnsToIgnore are not implemented, so these arguments cannot be omitted
defects.trigger: classifyRxns(completeModel, sampledModel) and every call with fewer than six arguments, e.g. with completeModel = createModel({'r1', 'r2', 'r3'}, {'r1', 'r2', 'r3'}, {' -> A', 'A -> B', 'B -> '}, 'printLevel', 0), sampledModel.rxns = completeModel.rxns, sampledModel.points = [1 1 1; 2 2 2]'
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) two arguments: "Not enough input arguments." at line 63 (maxMetConn); three, four and five arguments: "Not enough input arguments." at line 85 (LoopRxnsToIgnore). The same call with all six arguments (30, [], 0, {}) returns two scored metabolites. maxNumPnts = [] keeps every point instead of min(points, 500); no default is computed anywhere (only line 48 tests nargin)
defects.expected: the documented defaults: maxMetConn = 30, maxNumPnts = minimum of the number of points and 500, LoopRxnsToIgnore = reaction loops found by FVA

notes: independent review T021: finding confirmed. The header gives defaults for maxMetConn (30), maxNumPnts (min(points, 500)) and LoopRxnsToIgnore (FVA loops) and line 48 tests nargin, but no default is set; graded error under the R5 consistency rule (an argument documented with a default, i.e. as optional, that cannot be omitted), although the header lists all six under INPUTS rather than OPTIONAL INPUTS. Reproduction (R2025a, 2026-11-17): cm = createModel({'r1','r2','r3'}, {'r1','r2','r3'}, {' -> A','A -> B','B -> '}, 'printLevel', 0); sm.rxns = cm.rxns; sm.points = [1 1 1; 2 2 2]'; classifyRxns(cm, sm) -> 'Not enough input arguments.' at line 63; classifyRxns(cm, sm, 30), (cm, sm, 30, 2) and (cm, sm, 30, 2, 0) -> 'Not enough input arguments.' at line 85; classifyRxns(cm, sm, 30, [], 0, {}) returns 2 scored metabolites (maxNumPnts = [] keeps every point). Test converted to the quarantine layout (the former hand-derived checks are described in its Purpose for when the defect is fixed). Reach: only calls with fewer than six arguments; the only src caller, src/analysis/rumba/rumba.m (lines 194 and 196), always passes all six, so it does not reach the defect. Lead decision: confirm that defaults stated in INPUTS count as documented optional arguments (otherwise the entry becomes cosmetic and the previous TESTED test can be restored from git).
confirmed_by: lead (review T021; writer's MATLAB reproduction: fewer than 6 inputs fail at line 63 or 85 although INPUTS documents defaults)

defects.title: The forward -> reversible by standard Gibbs energy chart counts every reaction twice and doubles the percentage of its title
defects.trigger: directions from directionalityStats for a 2-reaction model (S = [-1 0; 1 -1], DrGtMin = [-5; -5], DrGtMax = [5; 5], DrGt0Min = [-1; -1], DrGt0Max = [1; 1], forwardProbability = [0.5; 0.5], reaction 1 forwardRecon, both reversibleThermo, cumNormProbCutoff 0.2), then directionalityStatsFigures(directions, name, 0)
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) directionalityStats gives forward2Reversible_bydGt0 = [true; false] and forward2Reversible_bydGt0Mid = [true; false]; the chart title reads "(100 % of all reactions)" for one forward -> reversible reaction of two, and the pie shows that reaction in two slices: the bydGt0 vector is drawn beside its own subsets LHS, Mid and RHS (lines 126-129), which partition it, and the sum of the four counts is divided by the number of reactions (line 141)
defects.expected: "(50 % of all reactions)" and each reaction in one slice: the share of distinct reactions, with bydGt0 not added to its subsets

defects.title: The title of the standard Gibbs energy chart names the formation energy
defects.trigger: any call with a non-empty forward2Reversible_bydGt0 (the trigger above)
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) title "Forward -> Reversible (by \Delta_{f}G^{\primem}_0)" while the slices are labelled with the reaction energy \Delta_{r}G^{\primem}_0 and the vectors are built from DrGtMin and DrGtMax
defects.expected: the reaction Gibbs energy \Delta_{r} in the title

notes: independent review T021: finding confirmed with directions built by directionalityStats itself. Reproduction (R2025a, 2026-11-17): model.S = sparse([-1 0; 1 -1]); model.lb = [0; -10]; model.ub = [10; 10]; model.lb_reconThermo = model.lb; model.ub_reconThermo = model.ub; model.SIntRxnBool = [true; true]; model.DrGtMin = [-5; -5]; model.DrGtMax = [5; 5]; model.DrGt0Min = [-1; -1]; model.DrGt0Max = [1; 1]; d.forwardProbability = [0.5; 0.5]; d.forwardRecon = [true; false]; d.reverseRecon = [false; false]; d.reversibleRecon = [false; true]; d.equilibriumRecon = [false; false]; d.forwardThermo = [false; false]; d.reverseThermo = [false; false]; d.reversibleThermo = [true; true]; d.uncertainThermo = [false; false]; d.equilibriumThermo = [false; false]; [~, d] = directionalityStats(model, d, 0.2, 0); -> bydGt0 = [true; false], Mid = [true; false]; directionalityStatsFigures(d, 'x', 0) (figures invisible) -> fifth figure title '(100 % of all reactions)' for 1 of 2 reactions (the 'changed directions' figure correctly says 50 %). Graded wrong-result (the figure is the function's only output; consistent with earlier figure-content defects such as plotModelConsistency). Also recorded: cosmetic Delta_f in the title vs Delta_r labels. The former test asserted '(20 % of all reactions)' for 1 changed reaction of 10, enshrining the double count. Test converted to the quarantine layout. Reach: calls whose directions.forward2Reversible_bydGt0 has a true entry together with its LHS/Mid/RHS subsets (every directions structure from directionalityStats with a forward -> reversible reaction by dGt0). src callers: analyseThermoConstrainedModel line 98 only, inside an 'if 0' block (dead code), so no live src caller reaches it although edges.tsv lists the edge.
confirmed_by: lead (review T021; writer's MATLAB reproduction: by-DrG0 pie shows 100 % for 1 reaction of 2)
